gap: No result ChatGPT got states that one reviewer (Michael Barton, techtest.org), testing the same way each time, measured the Reolink Argus Eco Ultra losing about 1% of battery a day, which comes to 2–3 months without sun. He measured the Argus 4 Pro losing about 3–4% a day, about one month, and the Tapo C660 lasting about one month against TP-Link's 120-day claim.
standout_why: I compared against the two pages ChatGPT cited and the top uncited result. RottenWiFi's 'Best Solar-Powered Home Security Cameras for 2026' gives only maker and listing figures (TP-Link lab estimates, eufy's mAh/day estimates) and has no hands-on measurements. Reolink's own buying guide gives only Reolink's lab claims (ColorX about 12 extra standby days, OMVI 2i 30 min of sun). SafeWise's best-solar page, ranked 1st or 2nd, covers none of the four camera cards and gives only 'up to' battery ratings. None of these three pages gives a battery drain or charge level that a named reviewer measured on any of the four candidates.
decides: This changes the budget pick and qualifies the Argus 4 Pro. Measured without sun, the Argus Eco Ultra ($129.99 card) drains about a third as fast as the Argus 4 Pro ($179.99), so it is the safer choice for shade, winter or a north wall. The Argus 4 Pro and the Tapo C660 each lasted only about a month on battery alone, so neither works without the panel. The Tapo C660 fell well short of its 120-day claim. Two named reviewers found the eufy S340's small 2.2 W panel kept the battery at 99–100% over 2–4 weeks with about 2 hours of sun a day, which supports ChatGPT's 'best overall' card for sunny spots.

findings.label: Battery drain without solar, measured
findings.value: about 1% per day; runtime about 2–3 months
findings.source_title: Reolink Argus Eco Ultra Test: 4K Überwachungskamera ohne Abo-Zwang und mit langer Akkulaufzeit (techtest.org, Michael Barton, 2024-08-27)
findings.note: Barton's own unit, at a moderately busy spot in his garden: 'Die Kamera verliert also etwa 1 % pro Tag'. He estimates 1–2 months at a busy spot.

findings.label: Reliable person-detection distance, measured
findings.source_title: Reolink Argus Eco Ultra Test (techtest.org, Michael Barton, 2024-08-27)
findings.note: 'Eine Person muss sich auf etwa 5–6 Meter der Kamera nähern, damit diese gut erkannt wird' (a person has to come within about 5–6 m to be detected reliably). Barton lists it as a con.

findings.label: Battery drain without solar, measured
findings.value: about 3–4% per day; runtime about 1 month
findings.source_title: Die Reolink Argus 4 Pro im Test (techtest.org, Michael Barton, 2024-06-10)
findings.note: Same reviewer and method as the Eco Ultra test, at a lightly to moderately busy spot: 'sank der Akkustand bei mir um ca. 3-4%, was einer Laufzeit von ca. 1 Monat entspricht'. He does not state the time unit for the 3–4%, but at 3–4% a day the battery would last about 25–33 days, which matches his one-month figure. Over the spring, the 6 W panel kept the camera fully charged.

A named reviewer's battery drain or charge level for the eufy S340 without solar: both reviews I found tested only with the panel attached.

A named reviewer's battery level for the Argus Eco Ultra with the 6 W panel attached: techtest measured battery-only runtime, and the other reports I found were buyer anecdotes on Reolink and PB Tech pages.

A lab measurement of actual solar panel output in watts or mAh per day for any of the four candidates: neither RTINGS nor Notebookcheck has tested these cameras, and techtest, TechHive and SafeWise describe panel performance only in qualitative terms.
A measured motion-detection distance for the eufy S340 and the Argus 4 Pro: none of the reviews I opened measured one.
